security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel checks for Sstc extension presence (via ISA string or DT) and assumes stimecmp-driven STIP semantics, but firmware has set menvcfg.STCE=0 (or henvcfg.STCE=0 for VS-mode), causing the hardware to behave as if Sstc is not implemented — STIP in sip becomes execution-environment-controlled rather than stimecmp-reflected, yet kernel code still treats STIP as read-only and timer-driven.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: kernel code that tests Sstc extension availability (riscv_isa_extension_available, __riscv_isa_ext, DT property) and branches into stimecmp-based timer path without also reading menvcfg.STCE / henvcfg.STCE to confirm the enable bit is set
security_spec.summary: Kernel relying solely on Sstc extension probe without verifying menvcfg.STCE==1 may misread STIP behavior, causing lost or spurious timer interrupts and potential scheduler hang

findings.finding: Sstc static branch is enabled based solely on riscv_isa_extension_available(NULL, SSTC) without reading menvcfg.STCE to confirm firmware has enabled stimecmp for S-mode. When menvcfg.STCE=0, subsequent csr_write(CSR_STIMECMP, ...) in riscv_clock_event_stop/riscv_clock_next_event will raise illegal-instruction exceptions because the hardware behaves as if Sstc is not implemented.

spec_citations.excerpt: The STCE bit enables stimecmp for S-mode when set to one. When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception, STCE in henvcfg is read-only zero, and STIP in mip and sip reverts to its defined behavior as if this extension is not implemented.

findings.finding: Direct csr_write(CSR_STIMECMP, next_tval) under the static_branch_likely(&riscv_sstc_available) guard, which was enabled solely on ISA string check. If menvcfg.STCE=0, this write to stimecmp from S-mode triggers an illegal-instruction exception, crashing or hanging the calling CPU.

spec_citations.excerpt: When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception

findings.finding: Reads CSR_STIMECMP based only on riscv_has_extension_unlikely(RISCV_ISA_EXT_SSTC) without checking menvcfg.STCE. On resume from suspend, if firmware cleared menvcfg.STCE during the suspend cycle (e.g. for security policy or as part of a firmware update), the kernel will trap on the csr_read.

spec_citations.excerpt: When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception

findings.finding: Writes to CSR_STIMECMP during resume based solely on ISA extension check. If firmware has menvcfg.STCE=0 (e.g. cleared during suspend), the csr_write traps and the resume path fails, potentially leaving the CPU in an inconsistent state.

spec_citations.excerpt: When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception

findings.finding: Sets t->sstc_enabled = true based on riscv_isa_extension_available(NULL, SSTC) without checking henvcfg.STCE (or menvcfg.STCE which gates it). When menvcfg.STCE=0, henvcfg.STCE is read-only zero per spec, so vstimecmp CSR accesses in kvm_riscv_vcpu_timer_restore/sync/save will trap in HS-mode, crashing the VCPU run path.

spec_citations.excerpt: When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero ... STCE in henvcfg is read-only zero, and STIP in mip and sip reverts to its defined behavior as if this extension is not implemented.

The Sstc extension adds the STCE (STimecmp Enable) bit to henvcfg CSR ... When STCE bit is henvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp (really vstimecmp) when V=1 raises a virtual-instruction exception, and VSTIP in hip reverts to its defined behavior as if this extension is not implemented.

findings.finding: Writes to CSR_VSTIMECMP guarded only by t->sstc_enabled. When menvcfg.STCE=0 forces henvcfg.STCE read-only zero, vstimecmp is inaccessible from HS-mode just as stimecmp is from S-mode, causing an illegal-instruction trap on VCPU load.

spec_citations.excerpt: When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception, STCE in henvcfg is read-only zero

findings.finding: csr_write(CSR_VSTIMECMP, -1UL) on VCPU put path, guarded only by t->sstc_enabled. With menvcfg.STCE=0 making henvcfg.STCE read-only zero, vstimecmp is inaccessible, and this write traps during VCPU context switch, causing a host crash.

findings.finding: SSTC is registered with __RISCV_ISA_EXT_DATA (no validate callback), unlike SVADU which has a validate callback via __RISCV_ISA_EXT_DATA_VALIDATE. No menvcfg.STCE check exists anywhere in the extension probe path. By contrast, extensions like smnpm/ssnpm declare riscv_xlinuxenvcfg_exts as subset, and SVADU has riscv_ext_svadu_validate. SSTC has neither, meaning the kernel trusts the ISA string unconditionally without verifying firmware enablement.

spec_citations.excerpt: This extension adds the STCE bit to the menvcfg and henvcfg CSRs.
When the Sstc extension is not implemented, STCE is read-only zero.

findings.finding: cfg->henvcfg |= ENVCFG_STCE is set based on the guest ISA string (riscv_isa_extension_available(isa, SSTC)), not on host menvcfg.STCE. If menvcfg.STCE=0, this write to henvcfg.STCE is a no-op (the bit is read-only zero), so the guest VCPU will see STCE=0 in henvcfg while its ISA string advertises Sstc. The guest kernel would then encounter the same vulnerability pattern when it tries to use stimecmp. This is a virtualization correctness bug: the guest ISA string and the actual henvcfg state are inconsistent.
